title: Canto 3:  The Status Quo - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 3
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 3

3.1

Title: ‘The Disrobing of Draupadī’.

Artist: Attributed to Nainsukh (1710-1778). India, Punjab Hills, Basohli, ca. 1765

Source: Website Devi Smithsonian Museum

3.2

Title: “Kṛṣṇa as Venugopal”.

Artist: Giri Raj Sharma.

Source: exoticindiaart.com, used with permission.

3.3

Title: The picture shows Lord Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna engaging in the battle at Kurukṣetra.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

3.4

Title: The picture is a Hindu vintage image of Lord Viṣṇu.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

3.5

1. Title: The first painting represents Hanumān at the feet of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā.

Artist: K. Venkatappa.

Source: Wikipedia.org

3.6

Title: “The Equivalence of Self and Universe”.

Artist: Moslim artist Bulaki, Jodphur, 1824.

Source: Mehrangarh Museum Trust, Mehrangarh.org

3.7

Title: Kṛṣṇa killing the demon Mura

Artist: Original folio of a Bhāgavata Purāṇa manuscript. Pre-Mughal c.a. 1550

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

3.8

Title: “The deity Viṣṇu reclines on the coil of the great serpent Ṣeṣa, while the four-headed Brahmā springs from his navel. Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu’s consort, caresses his feet with devotion”.

Artist: Chamba, Pahari. Date c.a. 1780-90.

Location: The National Museum, New Delhi 47.110/605

Source: Wikipedia.org

3.9

Title: The image is a collage of a Brahmā picture of a pendant of Exotic India Art (used with permission) and a background from a painting titled: ‘Brahmā honors Kṛṣṇa’. Page from a dispersed series of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Story of Lord Viṣṇu), India, probably Delhi-Agra region, ca. 1525-40. Ter beschikking gesteld door Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Sources: exoticindiaart.com & Philadelphia Museum of Art

3.10

Title: “Brahmā with Sarasvatī”

Artist: From an illustration to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, ca. 1793, Paris, Manuscripts orient.

Source: Wikimedia.org

3.11

Title: The picture is a blend by Anand Aadhar of two paintings.

One is titled: ‘Clock’ and is © by Vlad Holst (used with permission),

the other is titled: ‘Gopala’ and is © by Johannes Ptok (Aka Janmanalaya)

Artist: Anand Aadhar Prabhu

Artist: Vlad Holst

Artist: Johannes Ptok (Aka Janmanalaya)

Source: Ten Dreams.org, Consciousart gallery & Ptok.se

3.12

Title: Four Kumāras

Artist: The image was donated by the Editor in Chief, Sri Vasudeva Sarana Upadhyaya, of the Sri Sarvesvara Press, Sri Nimbarkacarya Pitha, Salemabad, Rajasthan, India.

Source: Wikipedia.org

3.13

Title: Contemporary picture ‘Varāha Avatāra’

Source: exoticindiaart.com, used with permission.

3.14

Title: ‘Viśvāmitra and Menaka’ dated 1890

Artist: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Maharaja Fateh Singh Museum, Vadodara, Gujarat & Wikipedia.org

3.15

Title: The on fair use based picture, titled “Gate to Vaikuṇṭha”,

is a blend by Anand Aadhar of two pictures.

One is a tourist snapshot of an Indian temple entrance with Jaya and Vijaya as guards;

the second is a Hubble telescope picture of the Tarantula Nebula.

Artist: Anand Aadhar Prabhu

Sources: wikipedia.org & Alchetron.com

3.16

Title: The digitally enhanced picture of the praying Kumāras is a mural in Mayapur, India.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

3.17

Title: ‘Karma’

Artist: © Wim Kuenen (Prema, used with permission).

Source: Prema.exto.nl

3.18

Title: “Viṣṇu as Varāha saves the Earth”

Artist: Himalayan foothills, Chamba, Pahari region, north India c.a. 1740

Source: British Museum, britishmuseum.org

3.19

Title: Lord Varāha being worshiped

Artist: © Vlad Holst, used with permission

Source: Ten Dreams.org

3.20

Title: “Viṣṇu on Ananta”; around early 19th century, Indian manuscript

Source: The University of Michigan Museum of Art, umma.umich.edu

3.21

Title: ‘The painting of Viṣṇu appearing in the sky on the back of Garuḍa’

Type: Sacred Art of India

Artist: © Dominique Amendola, used with permission

Source: dominiqueamendola.com

3.22

Title: The parade of Vedic royalty traveling with their retinue is factually

a detail of a picture illustrating the Rāmāyaṇa. It is titled:

“Vālmīki’s Narration, Page from the Araṇyakāṇḍa, 3rd Book of the Rāmāyaṇa,

Verses 19-34”, Indian, Punjab Hills, Kangra, ca. 1830-1840

Source: Ackland Museum of Art, ackland.org

3.23

Title: The painting suggests the dressing of Devahūti

Artist: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia.org

3.24

Title: The picture is a portrait of Lord Kapila

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

3.25

Title: The illustration is of a young Kapila talking to his mother Devahūti

Artist: B.K. Mitra

Source: Unknown

3.26

Title: The picture is a collage of Anand Aadhar of a wheel design of his own

and facial details of a stone temple carving, titled: “Trimūrti Ellora”

Artist: Anand Aadhar Prabhu

Source: Wikimedia.org

3.27

Title: The vintage image refers to the omnipresence of Kṛṣṇa in the heart of everyone

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

3.28

Title: The picture is a classical painting of Śrī Nārāyaṇa with Lakṣmī and Brahmā

Artist: Unknown

3.29

Title: The picture of the meditator in the sphere on the chakras

Artist: © Pieter Weltevrede

Type: ShareAlike Creativecommons.org

Source: sanatansociety.com & Wikimedia.org

3.30

Title: “Death of the Strong Wicked Man”.

Type: It is an illustration to Robert Bair’s ‘The Grave’, object 8

Artist: William Blake

Source: wikipedia.org & blakearchive.org

3.31

Title: The picture is a collage by Anand Aadhar of a vintage image of Viṣṇu

and an embryo study drawing by Leonardo da Vinci

Artist: Anand Aadhar

Source: Wikimedia.org

3.32

Title: The picture of the fruitive worker is by Vlad Holst

Artist: © Vlad Holst, used with permission

Source: Ten Dreams.org

3.33

Title: Picture of Devahūti fixing herself in the absence of het husband

Artist: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia.org
